The answer is C, about a 15-fold increase. Maddison and Penn World Table data put Japan's real, PPP-adjusted GDP per capita at roughly $3,000 in 1950 and $38,000–$40,000 in 2016, a rise of about 12–13 times. That is closer to 15-fold than to 10-fold. The team note's figure of about $8,000 for 1950 doesn't match those series, which is why I'm not changing my answer.

CONFIDENCE: 66
